glosses: To waste, lavish, splurge; to spend lavishly or profusely; to dissipate.

examples.text: 1886, Cora Pearl, Memoirs. "I have squandered money enormously.... I ought to have saved, but saving is not easy in such a whirl of excitement as that in which I have lived."

1746, Benjamin Franklin, Poor Richard's Almanac
Dost thou love life? Then do not squander time, for that's the stuff life is made of.
As the game opened up, Bolton squandered a fine opportunity to equalise - Chris Eagles shooting straight at Szczesny - but then back came Arsenal.

glosses: To wander at random; to scatter.

examples.text: […]The Wiſe-mans folly is anathomiz’d / Euen by ſquandring glances of the foole.

glosses: Poner en peligro o exponer a un riesgo.
Arriesgarse a decir algo dudoso y/o atrevido.
Seguir un curso de acción en el que hay gran riesgo, especialmente de la integridad física.
